newsitem.title: UK: Clyde Blowers buys Bergemann units.
newsitem.headline: Clyde Blowers buys Bergemann units.

text.p: Clyde Blowers Plc said on Thursday it intended to buy Bergemann Germany and the assets of Bergemann USA, both part of the Deutsche Babcock AG Group, for 17.1 million stg.
It said it would make a two-for-three rights issue to raise 12 million stg, underwritten by Guinness Mahon & Co Limited.
The rights issue will be priced at 265 pence per share.
Clyde Blowers also said its pretax profits for the year ending August 31, 1996 were estimated to be 2.312 million stg, with earnings per share of 20.4 pence.
It said the final dividend was forecast to be 5.33 pence per share, making a total of eight pence per share, a rise of 33 percent on the year earlier.
Clyde Blowers said the acquisition should give the combined group world leadership in the sootblowing equipment market.

"There are substantial opportunities for cost reductions and margin enhancement utilising the complementary geographic and technical strengths" of the two companies, Clyde Blowers chairman Jim McColl said in a statement.

Clyde Blowers added there would be an exceptional charge of approximately one million stg in accounts for the financial year ending August 31, 1997, relating to reorganisation costs resulting from the deal.
It said there were also "opporutnities for margin enhancement by stringent application of more rigorous contract pricing criteria to future supplies of new equipment."
